Be a patsy. If you are executed, the Alpha Wolf is not. Don't be afraid to die this way, since it gives the Alpha Wolf a day of safety. Furthermore, if you can look so execution-worthy that characters like the Hunter or Ravenkeeper use their ability on you, then at least they are not using it on the Alpha Wolf. Even if you nominate the New in Town, you might look evil, but it prevents the Alpha Wolf from doing so.

If you are not bluffing as an Outsider, heap as much suspicion on the actual Outsiders as possible. They will usually be trusted by the good team, since it's obvious that a Baron is in play, and will need to be killed if you are to win.

One option is getting your Alpha Wolf to kill you early on - players who die early at night are usually considered good, and you can use this position of trust to go around and talk to players, gathering information and feeding it back to the evil team, while also spreading misinformation. Whilst any Minion can use this strategy, of course, the Baron is particularly suited, since your devastating ability has already been used.
You don't always have to be the fall guy. The last thing you want is for you to look evil and have the Alpha Wolf to kill themselves and have you as their only escape route!

minions.name: Evil Twin
minions.summary: The currently Villager-aligned twin’s execution wins for Werewolves, even if death is prevented. Villagers cannot win while both twins live.
minions.howToRun: Pair Evil Twin with an opposite-alignment player. On the first night, wake both, let them see each other, and show each the other’s character. Track each twin’s current alignment rather than assuming the Evil Twin character is always evil. If both become the same alignment, choose a new opposite-alignment twin and inform the pair. While both twins are alive and Evil Twin’s ability works, block Villager victory. If the currently Villager-aligned twin is executed while the ability works, Werewolves win even if protection prevents death. Apply Bill inversion once. A dead Evil Twin normally loses this ability unless another effect, such as Vigormortis or Bone Collector, preserves it.
examples: The paired Villager changes to Werewolf, making both twins Werewolves. Storyteller chooses a new Villager-aligned twin.
A Villager-aligned player holding the Evil Twin character is executed but survives through protection; Werewolves still win, subject to Bill.
tipsAndTricks: Say that the good twin is the Evil Twin. Say it again, and again, and again. After all, that's what the good twin will be doing!

Claim that you are the same character as the good twin. On the first night, you learn the character of the good twin, and they learn yours. This is a hint to help you know a character that is safe to bluff as.

Be passionate, not relaxed. Since the game end, and evil wins, whenever the good twin is executed, the good twin is almost always very vocal and insistent that they do not be executed under any circumstances.
Get the good twin executed, however you can. Give false information that indicates that your fellow evil players information is true. Give true information so that you look more trustworthy.

If you are the Alpha Wolf, cease killing at some stage, to pretend that the Alpha Wolf was executed that day. Normally, if the Alpha Wolf is executed, the game continues (the Evil Twin character says that while the Evil Twin is alive, 'Good can not win').

If you are the Alpha Wolf, feel free to try riskier bluffs that you may not otherwise feel fully capable of succeeding with. Since the game continues if you die, it matters less than normal if you are executed.

minions.name: Godfather
minions.summary: You start knowing which Outsiders are in play. If 1 died today, choose a player tonight: they die. [-1 or +1 Outsider]
minions.howToRun: At setup choose either one additional Outsider or one fewer Outsider, within the available script, and do not combine Godfather with Bill. Tell Godfather which Outsider characters are in play. If at least one player who counts as an Outsider dies during the day, including by execution or exile, wake Godfather that night to choose exactly one player to kill. A night death does not qualify.
examples: Two Outsiders die during the day; Godfather chooses one night victim.

minions.name: Mastermind
minions.summary: If the Alpha dies by execution and that would end the game, play one more day. Executing a good player then wins for Werewolves; otherwise Villagers win.
minions.howToRun: If the actual Alpha dies by execution and that death would otherwise end the game, suspend that win and play through one more night and day. On the extra day, an executed good player gives Werewolves the win; an executed evil player or no execution gives Villagers the win. If the chosen player survives execution, apply the execution outcome based on that player’s team. Apply any active Bill inversion once to the final result.
examples: The Alpha dies by execution. The next day nobody is executed, so Villagers win.

minions.name: Poisoner
minions.summary: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned tonight and tomorrow day.
minions.howToRun: Each night wake Poisoner to choose any player, including themself. That player is poisoned from the choice through the following day. They may still be woken and appear to act, but their ability has no effect and their information may be false. An attempted once-per-game use is spent. When the effect expires, remove only this Poisoner source; another active poison source continues to apply.
examples: A poisoned Hunter attempts their once-per-game shot. It fails, and the use is spent.
tipsAndTricks: Identifying targets for poison is vital. Characters who get information over several nights like the Seer or Gravedigger are great choices if you can find them. You can also make your choice based on the player; players who are strong leaders and rallying the good team or players who are quiet and trying not to attract attention are good options.

Undermine players who trust each other by poisoning the characters getting key info in that clique. If a group is rallying around an Gravedigger, you can turn the entire group on someone innocent by poisoning them at the right time.
Co-ordinate with your Alpha Wolf so that you are not selecting the same players - unless they are a character like the Ravenkeeper, you'll just be wasting your poison for the day!

Targeting characters like the New in Town, Hunter or Mayor can be excellent, but only if they use their ability while they are poisoned. You'll need to convince them to use their ability, or time it right so that they are compromised at the moment they choose to activate.
It's risky, but you can poison your own Alpha Wolf, and use the lack of death for that night to bluff as the Bodyguard or Soldier. (You should probably warn your Alpha Wolf you're going to do this!)

If everyone is on board with the idea, try poisoning the Successor. If the Alpha Wolfchooses to kill themselves, the Successor will become the new Alpha Wolf... unless you poison them first! That way, you or a third Minion can become the new Alpha Wolfand keep the Successor in play. Just don't get your Alpha Wolfkilled while the Successor is still poisoned!

You will usually be more efficient as a Poisoner by selecting multiple targets around the town rather than focusing on one player for the entire game. You only really need to poison the Seer on the night they're checking your Alpha Wolf, for example - then you're free to mess with other characters. This method of poisoning is also more difficult to detect than sticking to one player.
On the other hand, if you only poison one player, that player might end up looking like the Village Idiot, perhaps hiding the real Village Idiot, or making it look like a Baron is in play.

On the first night, if you don't know who to poison, poison a player sitting next to the Alpha Wolf. You know which player is the Alpha Wolf, and on the off chance that an Empath is sitting next to the Alpha Wolf, you'll be giving some very damaging information to the good team.
Make use of your Spy! They know who the best targets are and can guide you in the right direction.

minions.name: Spy
minions.summary: Each night, you see the Grimoire. You might register as good & as a Villager or Outsider, even if dead.
minions.howToRun: Each night show Spy the current Grimoire. For each relevant check or target-sensitive ability, the Storyteller may register Spy as a Villager and a particular Townsfolk or Outsider, even while dead. The decision may differ between checks, but Spy remains an actual Werewolf Minion and does not gain the registered ability. Do not combine Spy with Bill.
examples: New in Town is nominated by Spy; if Spy registers as Townsfolk for that interaction, the nomination may trigger New in Town.
tipsAndTricks: You will usually register as a good player to characters like the Empath, Chef, and Gravedigger. Thanks to this, you will be able to gain the trust of good players much more easily than the other evil characters.

You also have access to information that is hard to guess or obtain as an evil player, like player's characters. This makes you an especially potent Housekeeper, Gravedigger or Ravenkeeper, since all of these characters learn that sort of information.

The Spy is particularly effective for bluffs that require more than one player. For example, you can claim to be the Housekeeper, Librarian or Ravenkeeper and back up your Alpha Wolf's character claim.
You are the only evil player that can activate the New in Town ability. Players who die this way are usually the most trusted characters in the game.

minions.name: Successor
minions.summary: With at least five living non-Travelers immediately before Alpha death, you immediately become that Alpha. A Fang Gu jump takes precedence, leaving you Successor.
minions.howToRun: When the Alpha dies, count living non-Travelers immediately before that death. If there were at least five and Successor is alive and able to act, immediately change Successor into the same Alpha type and show them their new character that night. Fenrir self-kill passes to Successor ahead of another Minion. If Fang Gu dies as part of a successful jump to an Outsider, the Outsider becomes Fang Gu and Successor remains Successor; this is the Fang Gu–Scarlet Woman jinx adapted to Wolf’s Bane.
examples: Six non-Travelers are alive. Fenrir kills themself; Successor immediately becomes Fenrir.
Fang Gu attacks an eligible Outsider and dies instead. The Outsider becomes Fang Gu; Successor stays a Minion.
tipsAndTricks: The Successor is at her strongest when you co-ordinate with the Alpha Wolf and figure out a strategy that you both like, since the Alpha Wolf can safely die. Maybe you accuse the Alpha Wolf of being evil, and the Alpha Wolf does everything possible to make the good team think they are indeed evil? This makes you look very good, and trustworthy. Maybe the Alpha Wolf kills themselves of a night time and claims to be the Ravenkeeper, saying that you are the character you say you are. Maybe the Alpha Wolf accuses you of being evil, but does so unconvincingly, so that you look good by comparison. Maybe you and the Alpha Wolf both claim to be the same character, such as the Mayor? After all, "one of you must be the Mayor", right? It doesn't matter which one of you dies, since the game continues with a living Alpha Wolf either way.

In the early game, staying alive is more important for you compared to other Minions. Whist it doesn't really matter if the Baron, or Poisoner dies early (since they can often cause a lot of disruption early in the game), you will need to survive until the end of the game if you intend to become the Alpha Wolf at some point. Waiting, listening, then claiming to be a character that you know is not in play often achieves this best.

Timing is important. Remember that if fewer than five players are alive when the Alpha Wolf dies, the game is over and good wins. If your Alpha Wolf has a lot of heat on them, and you think that they won't survive to the final day, take action and get your Alpha Wolf killed while five or more players are still alive... before it's too late.

Whilst you are the Successor, you will not register as the Alpha Wolf. So, if you can get yourself confirmed as such by good characters, such as the Hunter or the Fortune Teller, then become the Alpha Wolf at a later stage, then the good team will be very confused about the identity of the real Alpha Wolf, as their information won't add up.

If the Alpha Wolf is playing well, and seems to be trusted by the good team, there is no need to use your ability. You can play the normal Minion role of spreading false information, breeding distrust among the good players and generally being troublesome whilst ignoring your character ability.

minions.name: Advocate
minions.summary: Each night, choose a living player (different from last night): if executed tomorrow, they do not die.
minions.howToRun: Each night choose one living player, including Advocate themself, but not the player chosen the previous night. If that player is executed tomorrow while Advocate’s ability works, the execution occurs but the protected player does not die. A Zombuul that only registers as dead remains living for this choice. If Advocate is impaired during the effect, protection pauses.
examples: Advocate protects themself; they are executed tomorrow but survive, so death-triggered abilities do not fire.

Alpha Wolfs.name: Fang Gu
Alpha Wolfs.summary: The first Outsider your attack would kill becomes an evil Fang Gu and you die instead. This jump happens once per game; Successor stays Successor.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: Add one Outsider at setup in place of a Townsfolk. Each night except the first, wake Fang Gu to choose a player. On the first attack that would kill a player who counts as an Outsider, kill the original Fang Gu instead, make the attacked Outsider alive, evil, and the new Fang Gu, and mark the once-per-game jump as used for the rest of the game. A protected target that would not die does not cause a jump. Show the new Fang Gu their new character and evil alignment, but do not reveal the Minions to them. On later nights, Outsider attacks cause ordinary deaths. The new Fang Gu does not attack again in the same night. If Successor is in play, it remains Successor rather than creating two Alphas.
examples: Fang Gu attacks an unprotected Outsider. Original Fang Gu dies; the Outsider becomes an evil Fang Gu and remains alive.
Fang Gu attacks a protected Outsider. The Outsider survives and no jump occurs.

Alpha Wolfs.name: Fenrir
Alpha Wolfs.summary: Each night after the first, kill a player. If you kill yourself with this ability, Successor claims the handoff if eligible; otherwise Storyteller chooses a living Minion to become Fenrir.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: Each night except the first, wake Fenrir to choose one player. If Fenrir chooses themself and the kill succeeds, Fenrir dies. If an eligible Successor is alive and able to act, immediately change Successor into Fenrir. Otherwise the Storyteller chooses one living Minion to become Fenrir immediately. If no Minion can take over, there is no living Alpha and Villagers win, subject to Bill inversion and any other active win-blocking ability. The new Fenrir does not attack again that night.
examples: Fenrir kills themself with Successor in play and six non-Travelers alive. Successor becomes Fenrir.
Fenrir kills themself with no living Minion available. Villagers win if no other rule delays or changes that result.
tipsAndTricks: There are many strategies for evil players, particularly the Alpha Wolf, that are covered in more detail in Player Strategy section. Generally speaking, as the Alpha Wolf, you want to look trustworthy, spread false information where possible, get your Minions to confirm that you are a good player, and sacrifice them when needed. Take a look at this section for more information.

Stay alive during the day at all costs. Even in games with three Minions, do not assume there is a Successor in play. (However, if you talk to your Minion(s) and you learn that there is, then ignore this advice!)

If you are under suspicion, night time suicide is always an option. Killing yourself and passing the Alpha Wolfhood to a Minion that is looking more trustworthy robs you of the support of their continued voting power, but survival is more important. You can also do this when there is no suspicion on you - people tend to trust players that die at night. Either way, if you die at night, giving false information to the good team the day after, such as claiming to be the Ravenkeeper, can change the course of the game.
Your Minions are pawns to be sacrificed! Kill them! Kill them all! You're the only one that matters!

At the beginning of the game, the Storyteller will give you three possible bluffs to choose from. You can bluff as whatever you want, of course, but these few bluffs are safe. Since the Alpha Wolf can die at night, and pass the Alpha Wolfhood to a Minion, both the more passive and the more aggressive bluffs can be useful. If you are new to the game, or don't quite understand how certain characters work, either ask the Storyteller for help, or bluff as a more passive character, such as the Soldier or the Recluse. If you are more adventurous, more high-risk high-reward bluffs such as the Fortune Teller or Gravedigger can be risked.

A very bold strategy, to be employed on occasion when playing with players who are more familiar with the game, is to claim to be a character that you did not see as one of your bluffs. If you're bluffing as a character that's really in the game, then maybe the good team will assume that you're just a Baron who didn't learn any out of play characters, and kill the other players instead. Of course, they might decide that you're actually the Successor and execute you just to be on the safe side.

When choosing who to kill, you generally want to kill powerful, troublesome, information-gathering Villager sooner rather than later, such as the Empath, Gravedigger, Bodyguard or Hunter. Removing their information (or power) from the game early can help you later on. Every so often, deliberately keeping one of these Villager alive until the final day can double-bluff the good players. They may ask this player "If you are really the Fortune Teller, why are you still alive?", and kill them.

Also, when deciding who to attack at night, you are best killing the more trusted players earlier rather than later. A New in Town that everybody knows is the New in Town will never be executed, which decreases your odds of being executed later on. A pair of Outsiders that everybody believes are actually Outsiders will need to disappear, because they will not be executed either. On the final day, you will want at least one other player, preferably two, to be looking more suspicious than you.

Send your Minions out on information-gathering missions. Gather as much information as you can about who is who. This will help you avoid attacking troublesome characters like the Ravenkeeper or the Soldier, and the problems that consequently follow.

Talk to your Minions! Co-ordinate with them, by helping them bluff. Agree that one of you will look as evil as possible, while the other one will take the Alpha Wolfhood and survive to the end of the game. Find out what your Spy knows. Co-ordinate with your Poisoner so that you choose different players at night. Let your Baron run wild. Learn if your Successor's plan is to kill you, or keep you alive.

There are lots of reasons why you should register as an evil Alpha Wolf to good players. If this happens, don't despair! Maybe you can convince the group that Empath is Village Idiot? Maybe you can argue that you are that Fortune Teller's "red herring"?

If you don't want to kill one night, you can choose a dead player instead. This can also help you bluff well as the Soldier or the Bodyguard, as no death of a night-time makes it look like your Soldier or Bodyguard ability triggered. If no one is dead after the first day, there are no dead players to 'sink' a kill into, but if you're committed to bluffing as one of those characters, just ask your Poisoner pick you!

Alpha Wolfs.name: No Dashii
Alpha Wolfs.summary: Your nearest Townsfolk in each seating direction are poisoned, including dead Townsfolk, while your ability works.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: On the first night, find the nearest player who counts as Townsfolk in each seating direction from No Dashii, skipping Outsiders, Minions, and Travelers but not dead Townsfolk. Poison those two players while No Dashii has its ability. Recalculate immediately when seats, characters, or relevant registration changes; remove this poison from former neighbors and apply it to new ones. If No Dashii dies or loses its ability, its poison pauses or ends as appropriate. Each night except the first, wake No Dashii to choose a player to attack.
examples: A dead Townsfolk is the closest Townsfolk clockwise from No Dashii and remains poisoned.

Alpha Wolfs.name: Po
Alpha Wolfs.summary: After the first night, choose one player to attack or choose nobody to charge; after a no-one choice, you must choose three players on your next acting night.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: Each night except the first, wake Po. Normally Po may choose one player or explicitly choose nobody. Choosing nobody charges three attacks, even if Po is impaired; choosing a player whose death fails does not charge. On the next night Po acts, require three choices one at a time and resolve each in order before the next, including any Goon effect. Follow normal choice rules for repeated targets; a later attack on someone already dead has no further death effect. If Po misses a wake after charging, retain the charge until Po next acts. The first night never counts as choosing nobody.
examples: Po chooses nobody while poisoned. On the next acting night Po must choose three players, though poisoning then may make the attacks fail.

Alpha Wolfs.name: Pukka
Alpha Wolfs.summary: Act on the first night. Each choice poisons the new target; the previous target dies while still poisoned, then the Pukka poison clears.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: Each night, including the first, wake Pukka to choose a player. If Pukka can act, poison the new target immediately. Then attempt to kill the previous Pukka-poisoned target while that target is still poisoned; clear only this Pukka poison afterward if the death was attempted, while leaving any other poison sources intact, including when protection prevents death. Keep the poison through any death-triggered ability resolution before clearing it. If Pukka is impaired, its existing effect pauses and may resume when Pukka regains ability; a choice made while impaired creates no new poison. If Pukka does not wake because another role suppresses its wake, an existing previous victim can still die if Pukka retains its ability.
examples: Pukka poisons Sage one night. Next night Pukka poisons another player, then Sage dies while poisoned; Sage’s death information may be false.

Alpha Wolfs.name: Shabaloth
Alpha Wolfs.summary: After the first night choose two attack targets in order. Before a later Shabaloth wake, Storyteller may revive one player attacked the previous night, including someone already dead when attacked.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: Each night except the first, wake Shabaloth to choose two players one after another; resolve attacks in that order. Before each later Shabaloth wake, Storyteller may revive one dead player Shabaloth chose on the previous night, including someone already dead when chosen. A revived player regains their ability and a used once-per-game ability; a first-night-only ability runs on that revival night; another wake ability uses its ordinary slot, waiting until the following night if that slot has passed. Announce revival at dawn. Shabaloth cannot revive themself after their own death because their ability is no longer active.
examples: Shabaloth attacks a dead Professor and a living Townsfolk. On the next night Storyteller may revive Professor before Shabaloth wakes.

Alpha Wolfs.name: Vigormortis
Alpha Wolfs.summary: Minions killed by your attack keep their abilities while you live and each poisons one nearest Townsfolk neighbor. Remove one Outsider at setup.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: At setup remove one Outsider and add one Townsfolk; if there is no Outsider to remove, make no swap. Each night except the first, wake Vigormortis to attack one player. A Minion killed by this attack remains dead but keeps their ability while Vigormortis lives and has its ability. For each such Minion, Storyteller chooses one nearest Townsfolk clockwise or counterclockwise, skipping other character types but not dead Townsfolk, to poison. Recalculate the affected Townsfolk when relevant characters or seats change. If Vigormortis dies or loses its ability, the retained Minion abilities and poison ordinarily stop; the official Mastermind jinx preserves a Mastermind ability already granted by Vigormortis when Vigormortis dies.
examples: Vigormortis kills Poisoner. Poisoner remains dead but can act, and one nearest Townsfolk is poisoned while Vigormortis continues to empower that Minion.

Alpha Wolfs.name: Zombuul
Alpha Wolfs.summary: If nobody died today, attack tonight. The first time you would die, you appear dead but remain secretly alive; while apparently dead, use ordinary dead-player public rules.
Alpha Wolfs.howToRun: On the first would-be death while Zombuul has its ability, do not actually kill Zombuul, but announce a death, flip their public life marker, and mark them as apparently dead. This counts as a death today for Zombuul’s wake condition. They have one public dead vote token, cannot nominate, and are skipped as a living neighbor, but remain secretly alive for their own ability and victory. A second would-be death kills them for real. If nobody died today, wake Zombuul after the first night to choose one player to attack. Executing an already dead player without a new death does not block this wake. If Zombuul is impaired before their first would-be death, the first-death protection does not work; do not announce an apparently dead Zombuul as alive merely because it later becomes impaired.
examples: Zombuul is executed and appears dead. It does not attack that night; on a later no-death day, it may attack while still publicly dead.

travelers.name: Apprentice
travelers.summary: On your first night, Storyteller gives you a Townsfolk ability if Villager or a Minion ability if Werewolf; you remain a Traveler.
travelers.howToRun: On the first night after Apprentice enters play, Storyteller chooses and shows one ability from an eligible Townsfolk character if Apprentice is a Villager, or an eligible Minion character if Apprentice is a Werewolf. Apprentice gains that ability without becoming the character and may use it that night if its normal wake time occurs then. A first-night-only ability works on Apprentice’s own first night. A duplicate ability is possible, although a not-in-play character is usually simpler. If Apprentice changes alignment later, the already-gained ability remains; there is no second first-night grant. This follows from the ability being granted only on Apprentice’s first night. Apprentice remains a Traveler for character checks, exile, and player counts.
examples: A Werewolf Apprentice gains Assassin. They remain Apprentice but may use the Assassin ability according to its once-per-game timing.

travelers.name: Barista
travelers.summary: Storyteller chooses both recipient and effect nightly. The recipient learns whether they have true information and sobriety, or their ability works twice until dusk.
travelers.howToRun: Each night Storyteller chooses any player and one Barista effect. Privately tell that player, not Barista, which effect applies. Until dusk, either make them sober and healthy and guarantee true information despite ordinary false-information sources and registration, or let their ability work twice at its normal timing. An unused once-per-game ability may be used twice during the effect; an already-spent one may be used once more. Mandatory effects happen twice; optional abilities may be used twice. Clear the effect at dusk.
examples: Storyteller chooses a poisoned Empath for true-information mode. Empath is healthy and learns true information until dusk.
Storyteller chooses an Artist who already asked their question; Artist may ask once more before dusk.

travelers.name: Beggar
travelers.summary: Spend one token per execution vote. A dead player may voluntarily give you theirs; you learn that player’s alignment. Exile votes need no token.
travelers.howToRun: Beggar cannot vote in an execution without a token. A dead player may publicly give their unused vote token to Beggar; transfer it and privately tell Beggar that player’s alignment, allowing discretionary registration such as Recluse. Spend one token each time Beggar votes on an execution, even if the nomination fails. Exile votes require no token. If Beggar dies, discard collected tokens and give them the usual one dead vote token. Beggar remains sober and healthy.
examples: A dead player donates a token; Beggar learns their alignment privately and spends the token on one execution vote.
Beggar votes to exile a Traveler without spending a token.
tipsAndTricksGood: You definitely want to learn the alignment of at least one player, but don't get too greedy. Learning 1 or 2 players' alignments could mean that 1 or 2 good players can no longer vote - this is probably acceptable. But learning 5 players' alignment could mean that 5 good players can no longer vote - and that gives evil the majority vote at the next execution, granting evil the win. Gain a vote token or two... or three... but know when to stop.

Tell the truth about good players who give you their vote token. You trust them. They will probably trust you. Have a private conversation about your combined strategy for the future, and tell the group that they are good. You can trust whatever information this good player has due to their character ability, so use that to your advantage and let them help you decide who to vote for.

Lie about a good player who gave you their vote token. If you tell the group that a good player is in fact evil, the Alpha Wolf or its Minions may seek you out and tell you who they are, believing that you are evil too. This could be amazing information. Either way, you'll want to tell the group that you were lying before the game ends, and reveal your strategy to them, otherwise they may believe that you are evil, or that the good player who selflessly gave you their token is evil.

If an evil player is foolish enough or brave enough to give you their vote token, tell the truth about their alignment. Tell the group that the player is evil, and be prepared for that player to accuse you of being evil. Since it is rare for evil players to give their vote to a good beggar (but some will do so because it is so unexpected), you may find it difficult to convince the group that they are evil. It will be easier to convince the group if you can get a good player's vote token as well, as that good player will probably help you.

If an evil player has given you their vote token, you may want to lie about their alignment. Tell the group they they are good - this may convince the evil players that you are evil, and will encourage more evil players to give you their vote token. On the final day, you can reveal the truth.

You can't vote. So, when you do get a vote token, use it very, very wisely. This is especially important because you may have removed a good player's ability to vote when you took their token, which means that good has less voting power overall. Make your vote count by saving it until the final day, or waiting to use it when your vote will decide whether a player is executed or not.

Be proactive in getting players to give you their vote token. Ask. Demand. Bargain. Beg. Others will not usually volunteer to give you their token, because they have other things on their mind, but will often consider it if you pester them a little.
tipsAndTricksEvil: Learn the alignment of as many players as possible. Take vote tokens from as many players as possible. Even though by talking to the Alpha Wolf you can learn the alignments of all players quickly, the more players that give you their vote tokens, the more players will not be able to vote on the final day. You'll be able to vote as much as you want, and that is a powerful enough ability to win the game. Good players often don't realize how powerful their dead vote is - 1 player giving it away to an evil Beggar might not make much difference, but 4 players doing so will make a huge difference.

When good players give your their token, tell the truth about their alignment in order to gain their trust. If you publicly tell the group that a good player is good, that goes some way in confirming their legitimacy (and therefore their information), but you may be able to convince more players to give you their token. You can lie about their alignment at a later date.

Lie about good players' alignments, if you think that you can get away with it. It is much more common for good players to give their vote tokens to Beggars, so claiming that an evil player has done so is a difficult bluff. But, it is possible, and if you succeed, you have not only convinced the group of the illegitimacy of their information, you have gained a vote and convinced them of your goodness. The good player will kick and scream and do everything they can to convince the group that you are evil, so be prepared.

Lie about evil players alignment, if evil players give you their tokens. There is usually not much to be gained by telling the group that an evil player is evil, beyond making yourself look good. Sure, you'll get the benefit of looking more trustworthy (and maybe even getting another player to give up their vote token), but you've sacrificed the evil player to do so. The Chef, Empath, Investigator and Gravedigger in particular are very good at using the simple fact that one player is evil to deduce the alignment of several other players.

Tell the truth about evil players to build trust. But do so rarely. Very rarely. Since it is so unlikely that an evil Beggar would actually tell the group the truth about an evil player's alignment, when you actually do it, it may be believed. You'll want to make sure the payoff is worth it though. It can be worth it if the evil player was heavily suspicious anyway, or if the evil player was the third or fourth player to give you their vote token. In such circumstances, building the group's faith that you are good can give you the edge and keep you alive.

Use your vote wisely or throw it away. Either way, it doesn't really matter. What is important is that you look like you use your vote wisely, and that you save at least one vote token for the final day. The final day is all that really matters, so who you vote for before that point is mostly about making you look trustworthy so that you can survive until the final day.

Be proactive in getting players to give you their vote token. Ask. Demand. Bargain. Beg. Others will not usually volunteer to give you their token, because they have other things on their mind, but will often consider it if you pester them a little.

travelers.name: Bone Collector
travelers.summary: Once per game at night, restore a dead player’s ability until dusk, including spent once-per-game or first-night abilities.
travelers.howToRun: On a night after the first, Bone Collector may choose one dead player. The choice spends Bone Collector’s use. While Bone Collector is alive and able to act, the dead player regains their ability until the next dusk while remaining dead. A spent once-per-game ability is available again during this window; a first-night-only ability may run this night. End the borrowed ability at dusk or earlier if Bone Collector dies or loses the ability.
examples: Bone Collector restores a dead Artist; Artist may ask one question before dusk while still dead.

travelers.name: Bureaucrat
travelers.summary: Each night choose another player. Their execution votes count as three tomorrow while your ability works; exile votes stay normal.
travelers.howToRun: Each night wake Bureaucrat to choose a player other than themself, including a dead player. A repeat choice on consecutive nights is allowed. Until the next dusk, each execution vote cast by that player counts as three while Bureaucrat’s ability works; count all three publicly. If Bureaucrat dies or is impaired, the modification stops. Exile votes are unaffected.
examples: Bureaucrat selects a player who votes on two nominations; each vote counts as three.
tipsAndTricksGood: When picking who to give your extra votes to, prioritize living players. Dead players get a single vote for the rest of the game, and will be reluctant to spend it before a critical moment, even with your ability giving them an extra punch. (Similarly, be wary of characters like the Butler, who can have their voting restricted because of their ability.)

Find a good player you trust or who has been confirmed in some way, and pair up with them. Characters like a New in Town who has caused an execution or anyone confirmed by a Housekeeper are great options of trustworthy players you can work with. This also has the benefit of making you look good, as you are publicly aligning yourself with a good player.

Watch how people vote, especially the people you choose. Depending on who is on the chopping block, players will change their vote - it's very unlikely that a Minion would vote for their Alpha Wolf knowing they have 3 votes, for example. If a player doesn't take advantage of your power at a critical moment (or worse, does), then they are telling you a lot about their priorities and who they are aligned with.

Ask the town to help you choose who the person that receives your extra votes should be! If you don't have any strong leads on a reliable good player to trust, crowd-sourcing a solution will not only help the town trust you, but uncover good potential options for you to pick.

Communicate with the town about who you have picked - not only does keeping an open and honest policy help the town believe that you have a good alignment, but it helps the group when coordinating information and votes to get someone killed.

Deliberately lie about who you picked so that you can observe the behaviour of the player you 'picked'. While secretly giving your votes to a trustworthy player, pick someone who you want more of a read on, and see how they behave when they think they have extra voting power.

You are especially deadly on the final night - your ability means that one person can single-handedly kick off an execution. If you choose an evil player, good will have to work extra hard to make up the difference. Consider asking to be exiled before nominations begin - a good player may lose out on the extra kick you have to offer, but at least you know for sure your ability isn't going to cause more harm than good.

The Thief is your counterpart among Travellers, causing votes to count negatively... but if you both choose the same player, your abilities combine to give someone -3 votes! If you both trust the Thief and have a strong lead on an evil player, this can be a devastating way to undermine the evil team, cancelling out three evil votes!
tipsAndTricksEvil: Don't choose evil players ALL the time - that will look too suspicious. If you just choose the Alpha Wolf over and over again. the good team has reason to believe that you are evil, as good Bureaucrats tend to change their minds more often. Choose evil players MOST, but not all, of the time. This way, evil players will be getting the majority of the triple votes, but you look more trustworthy to the good team, allowing you to survive longer.

Another strategy is to choose good players until the perfect moment arises. This works best if the players you choose for the first half of the game are not only good, but believed to be good by the group. Choosing good players this way builds up a lot of trust in you, trust that you can betray at the last minute, by giving an evil player triple votes on the last day, or even at a similarly crucial point late in the game.

Choose an evil player on the final day. Although it might be tempting to choose a good player on the final day, so that you look more trustworthy, a good player having triple voting power is a huge danger to your team and far outweighs any benefits gained due to your angelic appearance. On the contrary, an evil player getting triple votes on the final day can win the game.

Choose dead evil players, if you can justify your reason for doing so. The dead are generally more trustworthy than the living, so giving a dead Minion triple votes not only helps your image, but gets that brutal extra two votes for the evil teams' desired nominee. A dead evil player with triple votes is really maximizing their offensive potential, as long as they actually are believed to be good.

travelers.name: Butcher
travelers.summary: After the first execution each day, you may nominate once more; the second nomination needs the ordinary half-of-living threshold.
travelers.howToRun: Immediately after the first execution of the day, including one where the executed player survives, offer Butcher one additional nomination. Butcher may nominate an earlier nominee. The second vote succeeds with at least half the living players, as for an ordinary execution; it need not beat the first tally. Resolve that execution, then close nominations. Butcher’s extra execution does not open a third nomination. Exile does not trigger this ability.
examples: A protected player survives the first execution. Butcher still nominates another player, who reaches the ordinary threshold and is executed.
tipsAndTricksGood: Only nominate players that you think you can execute. Executing 2 players per day is extremely helpful to the good team. Instead of 1 player dying during the day by the choice of the group and 1 player dying at night (by the choice of the Alpha Wolf), there will be 2 players dying per day by the choice of the group for every player that dies at night by choice of the Alpha Wolf.

During the normal voting process, pay attention to which players get a lot of votes, but are not executed, and which players don't get many votes, but are not executed. Players that get an overwhelming number of votes are unlikely to be the Alpha Wolf, since Minions rarely vote for the Alpha Wolf in such dangerous circumstances.

If the group keeps failing to vote for the players that you nominate, or if the group is talking about exiling you, then you can make a deal with them - you will nominate who they want you to nominate. Staying alive is better than being dead, even if it means that you go with the group's guesses instead of your own.

If there is an Evil Twin in the game, be much more frugal with your nominations. If the Alpha Wolf and the Evil Twin are both still alive when just 3 players are alive, it is possible that evil has already won.
tipsAndTricksEvil: Nominate. Nominate. Nominate. Vote. Vote. Vote. If you can secure an extra successful execution each day, then an evil victory is basically certain. Evil Butchers are incredibly dangerous.

You know who the Alpha Wolf is. Never nominate them using your ability. If even half the group votes, no other nominees can be nominated to exceed that tally, so there is no way to fix a foolish mistake.

If you really, really think that the good team trusts the Alpha Wolf player, nominate them using your ability. You need to be certain that even half the group won't vote for the Alpha Wolf, and be prepared for the good team to think that you are evil.
Nominate Minions using your ability. Or don't. Whatever you think is best.

If an Evil Twin is in play, co-ordinate with them to see if you can quickly get the number of living players to just 3 - the Evil Twin, the good twin, and the Alpha Wolf. At this point, evil has usually already won.

travelers.name: Gangster
travelers.summary: Once per day, with one nearest living neighbor’s agreement, kill the other. If agreement is refused, you may retry; an agreed attempt spends the use even if death is prevented.
travelers.howToRun: Identify Gangster’s nearest living neighbor clockwise and counterclockwise, skipping dead players and updating after seat changes. With Storyteller present, Gangster proposes killing one and asks the other to agree. If agreement is refused, no use is spent and Gangster may try again later that day. If either agrees, Gangster chooses the victim if both agree, then attempts the kill immediately; this spends the daily use even if protection prevents death. Reset at the next day.
examples: One neighbor refuses. Gangster later asks the other neighbor, who agrees; the first is killed.
A neighbor agrees, but the victim is protected from death. Gangster cannot attempt another kill that day.
tipsAndTricksGood: Find out the characters of your living neighbors. They will know you are the Gangster. It is best if you know their characters too. Learn what they are before making any rash decisions on who to kill.

Talk to each living neighbor. Convince them to "give you permission" to kill the other player, even if they think the other player is good. You are good, so being able to kill either living neighbor at any time is a powerful, and hopefully helpful, option to have. You can always choose not to kill either player, even if both players want you to kill the other.

If you can, kill every day. Just by playing the odds, killing two players per day (one by execution and one by Gangster) means that the good team is twice as likely to kill the Alpha Wolf and win. Even if you think both your living neighbors are good, it's worth it.

When choosing which player to kill, aim for evil players first. If you suspect someone of being evil, arrange for them to sleep with the fishes. If you don't really suspect either player of being evil, choose the player that has a character ability that seems less useful to the good team or the one that seems less willing to die.

If you believe that both your neighbors are good, and they both have character abilities that will continue to be useful for the rest of the game, don't kill today and don't ask for each player to kill the other. This way, they can both use their abilities to the fullest. You probably won't want to kill a Mayor, a Sage or a King, and if they die at night, then you will get to use your ability on a new living neighbor instead - your ability is also very useful, and it would be a shame to never use it.

If you think that a particular player is the Alpha Wolf (or even a Minion), then kill players that are sitting between you and them. Hopefully, in a day or two, you and the Alpha Wolf will be living neighbors and you can kill them with your ability.

Before the final day, request that the group exile you. An evil Gangster that is alive when just 3 other players are left alive can win the game for the evil team by agreeing with the Alpha Wolf to kill another player. Getting yourself exiled means that you won't be able to use your ability on the final day, but it will be a show of good faith to the good team. If the good team believes that you are good, they will look at your previous kills as the best choices of a good player, and not erroneously assume that you were just killing good players because you were evil.

Remember that you need your living neighbors to agree to use your ability. You can't just do it on their behalf. You'll need to make friends with them, and convince them that you are good and have the good team's interests at heart. They may not want you to use your ability, and with good reason.
tipsAndTricksEvil: If both your living neighbors are good, turn them against each other. If they both think that they are both good, they are unlikely to kill each other. Find some way to imply that at least one of them is evil, and one is likely to kill the other.

If one of your living neighbors is evil, they have every reason to want to kill the other living neighbor. The trick won't be in convincing them to do it, but in coming up with a good reason why. Talk to your evil neighbor and help them formulate a valid reason to tell the group since evil players that are too gung-ho in using the Gangster may appear evil. You can even act reluctant to kill the other neighbor and claim that you are doing so only because there is no better choice.

Get as many good players killed as possible. It doesn't matter how you do it. Every good player that dies is one fewer good player gaining information, one fewer player using an ability against the evil team,and one fewer good player voting.

Get any non-Alpha Wolf player killed. Even if Minions die due to your ability, that means that the final day is sooner, and evil's victory is sooner. Similarly, if Outsiders die to your ability, then evil is closer to winning. Don't be too concerned about what each player's character is... as long as they are not the Alpha Wolf, they are probably best dead.

Talk to any evil living neighbors before talking to any good living neighbors. Many players will want to kill the other player before that other player kills them, and talking to an evil neighbor first gives you a good excuse to kill the good player.

Every so often, it is better for the evil team if certain characters die by execution. Characters such as the Good Twin (see the Evil Twin) or the Saint lose the game for the good team if executed, so it is best to not kill them using your Gangster ability. Beware of pushing too hard here, though, as there's little reason for a good Gangster to not be willing to kill a Saint.

If you suspect that a good neighbor is about to be nominated and executed, don't kill them with your Gangster ability today. A death by the Gangster's ability doesn't count as an execution, and the day will continue afterwards. It is more helpful to the evil team if the day ends after the death occurs, so that the Alpha Wolf can't accidentally be executed today as well.

Choose players to die so that the distance between you and the Alpha Wolf is maximized. Since the Gangster can only kill living neighbors, the good players may have some very strong opinions on which of your living neighbors should die. If one of your living neighbors is the Alpha Wolf, they may put a lot of pressure on you to kill them, and while you can always choose not to, this may end up looking incredibly suspicious and reveal that you are evil and know who the Alpha Wolf is. It is best to avoid this situation by never neighboring the Alpha Wolf in the first place. When the Alpha Wolf is sitting 2, 3, 4, or more players away from you, keep it that way by killing players in the opposite direction.

travelers.name: Gunslinger
travelers.summary: Immediately after the first execution vote is tallied each day, you may kill one player who voted, even if the vote failed or tied.
travelers.howToRun: After the first execution vote of each day is tallied, before the next nomination or phase, ask Gunslinger whether to shoot. This is their only opportunity that day, even if the vote failed or tied. If they choose an actual voter, attempt to kill that player immediately, applying ordinary death protection. Exile votes are not execution votes and do not open this opportunity.
examples: The first nomination gets too few votes. Gunslinger may still immediately shoot a voter.
tipsAndTricksGood: Hot diggity, you're the Gunslinger! Enjoy it while you can!
Deaths caused by your ability are not executions, and as such, they don't cause the day to end, and nor does the character you shot get seen by the Gravedigger.

You get the opportunity to kill a player each day. Make the most of it, and remember to let the Storyteller know that you wish to use your ability. Doing so every day practically doubles the good team's chance of killing the Alpha Wolf. Normally, each day / night, 2 players die - one due to the Alpha Wolf attack, and one due to the daily execution. If you use your ability each day, two thirds of all deaths are chosen by the good team. These are great odds.

Pay attention to the vibe of the group. Sometimes, the good players will not want you to kill a player each day. If you go against their desires, they may Exile you as soon as they can. Pay attention and get your fingers off the trigger if you want to stay alive.

Pay attention to who isn't voting on the first nomination each day. Minions may be a bit laissez faire, but Alpha Wolf players quickly learn how dangerous it can be to vote when you are in play. Alpha Wolves will usually not vote if they think there is even a small chance that you will shoot them. Use this information to your advantage! By executing those players that seem fearful of voting, you may luck upon the Alpha Wolf. Or, you may startle the Alpha Wolf into voting, which gives you a chance of killing them single-handedly.
It's ok if a few innocent bystanders die. Don't be afraid to take out a supposed Gravedigger or a suspicious looking Recluse. As long as you kill a Minion or two as well, it was probably worth it.
You are the perfect way to deal with the Saint. They can't be executed? You don't execute!

If you live until just 3 players are left alive, be very wary of who you kill. The Alpha Wolf may try to psyche you out and get you to kill a Minion (or a good player), which will reduce the player count to just 2 players... and evil wins. Beware.

Ignore all of the above advice, and never use your ability. Sit. Wait. Watch. Be passive and silent and unassuming. Watch people's body language and listen to what arguments they are making. When you think that you know who the Alpha Wolf is, say nothing, and wait until that player votes on the first nomination of the day - then BOOM. Either you've won the game and have one very surprised dead Alpha Wolf, or you blew it and killed a nobody.
If there are 3 or more other Travelers in the game, you know that 1 of them is probably evil. It may be worth taking out an evil Traveler before they can do too much harm.
tipsAndTricksEvil: Just like a good Gunslinger, it is best if you kill each day. After all, you have insider information on who you should be killing and who you shouldn't, so go nuts. The more destruction you cause, the quicker that the game will get to the final day, and the more evil players will be alive compared to good, which gives your team greater voting power. Just like a good gunslinger though, listen to the group's opinion on what your actions should be, and don't go kill crazy unless they want you to.

Obviously, shooting the Alpha Wolf is a bad idea, unless you know you have a Successor. Luckily, you know who the Alpha Wolf is, so that won't be a problem. But should you kill Minions? That depends. If Minions are looking suspicious, and you think that they may get executed soon anyway, putting a cap in that Minion's arse may be the best option. Each Minion that you kill reduces the living players by one - and that means that an evil victory is one step closer. Killing a Minion that has already used their ability, such as a Baron or a Spy, is probably more helpful than keeping them alive. Killing a Minion that still has trouble to cause, such as a Poisoner or Successor is probably a mistake.
Of course, if you want to avoid shooting Minions, you'll have to learn who they are - be sure to coordinate with your Alpha Wolf!
Encourage the Alpha Wolf to vote. Since you'll not be killing them, they can vote freely. Tell the group that the players that are not voting are probably the Alpha Wolf.

You can play it safe, if you want to stay alive longer. Each day, kill the player that looks the most suspicious, regardless of what character they are claiming to be. This will ingratiate you with the good team, because it looks like you are trying to kill evil players. You can even ask the other players who they think you should kill. If the good players see you repeatedly killing the players that they want to kill, you'll live a long time.

You can throw caution to the wind, and kill the most dangerous, powerful good player to remove their ability from the game. If a Fortune Teller keeps getting fantastic information, and is believed to be trustworthy by the good team, you can quickly and easily neutralize that threat. The downside is that the good team will quickly vote to exile you afterwards. But there are situations where it is worth it. Another example is if a Soldier is in the game, and the good players overwhelmingly believe them, then you may foresee a troublesome final day where the Soldier is one of three living players. To avoid this situation, sacrificing yourself to remove the Soldier would be well worth it.

Use fear as a weapon. Nominate evil players, or bluff nominating evil players, and dare the good team to vote for it. You'll probably get exiled, but you can have some control over the execution for a day or two.

If the good players are foolish enough to keep you alive until just 3 players are left alive (not including Travelers), you've basically won. As soon as the first vote happens, kill a non-Alpha Wolf player and seize victory.

travelers.name: Judge
travelers.summary: Once per game, force a nomination made by another player to pass or fail, even just after its tally and before the next nomination.
travelers.howToRun: Once per game during a nomination made by someone other than Judge, or immediately after its tally before another nomination starts, Judge may force the result. A forced pass immediately executes the nominee regardless of tally, then resolve survival and victory rules; Butcher may still gain its extra nomination. A forced fail cancels this nomination’s votes and restores any earlier leading nomination as appropriate. The choice spends Judge’s use even if Judge is impaired.
examples: Judge forces another player’s nomination to pass with zero votes. The nominee is executed, though protection may keep them alive.

travelers.name: Matron
travelers.summary: Once each day, swap up to three pairs of seats consecutively. The new order persists; private game talks are limited to immediate seated neighbors.
travelers.howToRun: Once each day, Matron may choose up to three pairs of players to swap seats, one pair after another in a single opportunity. The same player may move more than once. Update the Grimoire and recompute seating-dependent abilities after each swap; the final arrangement persists until changed. While Matron’s ability works, players may discuss the game privately only with immediate seated neighbors and may not leave their seats to do so. Make reasonable accessibility accommodations for anyone who cannot move seats.
examples: Matron swaps two pairs and stops. They cannot return later that same day for a third swap.

travelers.name: Scapegoat
travelers.summary: If a same-team player would be executed, Storyteller may execute living Scapegoat instead; this replaces the execution, not merely its death.
travelers.howToRun: When a player would be executed, before applying that execution, Storyteller may choose a living Scapegoat who counts as the same alignment at that moment. Use approved per-check Spy/Recluse registration where applicable. Replace the original execution with Scapegoat’s execution and end nominations as an execution normally does. Apply death protection to Scapegoat; they may survive, but the original nominee was not executed. Exile is not execution.
examples: Saint is about to be executed, but same-team Scapegoat receives the execution instead. Saint lives and Saint’s loss does not trigger.
tipsAndTricksGood: Stay alive, however you can. Lay low and don't tempt the Alpha Wolf into attacking you. Avoid getting exiled until after your ability triggers. If you can live long enough for you to die in place of an executed player, that helps enormously. The Storyteller will often wait for the second half of the game for your ability to make your ability trigger, so be patient, and play it safe.

When the Storyteller declares that the players kill you instead of the normal executee, this is great! Talk to the player you saved in private. You know that they are good, and they know that you are good. Work together, vote together, and win together. Encourage them to tell you any information that they have due to their character ability, and any information that they have due to other private conversations they have had. Do whatever you can to keep this player alive, and save your vote for when they vote too.

Vote liberally, and try to convince others to do the same. If you execute an evil player, that's great! The Alpha Wolf will often bluff as a powerful information-gathering character that the good team doesn't want to execute, so taking a chance on executing the Fortune Teller might help your teammate enormously. If you execute a good player, you might be executed instead, which is what you want - you can keep that very real Fortune Teller alive!

After you have talked to the player whose life you saved, do whatever you can to convince the rest of the group that they are good. You have two publicly known facts to help you do this: Most Travelers are good. The odds that you are good, are good, therefore the odds that the player you saved is good, are good. Both you and the player you saved are the same alignment. If there is a Chef or Empath in play, their information would need to be congruent with you both being the same alignment. If an Investigator or Fortune Teller is in-play, their information may be incongruent with you both being evil. It is rare that a piece of information such as "two players are the same alignment" becomes publicly known, so use it to the full.

Beware of the Spy! If they get the votes, you, the poor, innocent, good Scapegoat might be executed instead! You at least learn that they weren't the Alpha Wolf when you were executed, so it's not all bad news!

Feeling devious? Go up to a player you don't trust and tell them you're evil. Convince them to get themselves executed so you can 'prove' you're on the same team - only to watch them get executed for their crime of believing you. One Minion (or even Alpha Wolf!) down.

To help convince the group that you are good, make the argument that another Traveler in the game is evil. Whether they are actually good or evil doesn't really matter to you. What does matter is that if the group thinks that one of them is evil, they will believe that you are good, because the chance of there being 2 evil Travelers is small. A group that believes that you are the good Traveler will keep you alive long enough for you to use your ability, and will believe that the player whose life you save is good too. And you never know, maybe the Traveler that you are throwing under the bus actually is evil after all!
tipsAndTricksEvil: Stay alive, however you can. So that the Alpha Wolf doesn't kill you, either talk to the Alpha Wolf to let them know that you are evil, or otherwise get a message to them. Avoid getting exiled no matter the cost. The Storyteller will almost always wait until the Alpha Wolf is executed for your ability to trigger, so you remaining alive until that happens will save the evil team from defeat. Sometimes, the Storyteller will make your ability trigger when a Minion is executed instead. If this happens, that's still great, because at least that Minion gets another night and day in the game.
You are that rare beast, an evil traveler who can prove themselves evil to their Alpha Wolf! If they get the votes and you're executed instead, they know that you must be their ally!

If the good team begins to think that you are evil, it may be best to die. Either get yourself exiled, or get the Alpha Wolf to kill you. If you live, and your ability triggers when a Minion dies, the good team will believe that the Minion you saved is in fact evil. This may give them all the information they need to deduce who the Alpha Wolf is.

When the Storyteller declares that the players kill you instead of the normal executee, this is great! Talk to the player you saved in private, just as if you were a good player. You can talk about the weather, football, whatever. As long as the good team believes that you are good, they will believe that the player you saved is good. If this player is the Alpha Wolf, this strategy could win you the game. If this player is a Minion, they get to keep their ability and their daily voting power.

If the game is near to a close, and you died in place of a Minion, it may be best if you look as evil as possible to the group. The following day, if just 3 or 4 players are left alive, the good team will probably execute the player you saved, believing them to be the Alpha Wolf. If you look evil, the good team thinks that the Minion is evil, and may not click that they are not in fact the Alpha Wolf. This strategy may still be useful if 5, 6, or even 7 players are still alive. Convincing the group to execute a Minion (again) at least means that they are not executing the Alpha Wolf, and good loses precious time and votes in the process.

Do whatever you can to convince the rest of the group that the player whose life you saved is good. This may be an uphill struggle, depending on the number of other Travelers in play. Since the group will know for a fact that you are both the same alignment, they may be able to use this information to prove or disprove other player's alignments. Pay attention, and focus on discrediting key players. For example, if the Alpha Wolf just got executed but saved by you, and the Empath is sitting next to you and knows that one of their neighbors is evil, you will need to completely discredit either the Empath, or their other living neighbor... otherwise it's curtains for team evil.

travelers.name: Thief
travelers.summary: Each night choose another player. Each execution vote they cast tomorrow subtracts one while your ability works; exile votes stay normal.
travelers.howToRun: Each night wake Thief to choose a player other than themself, including a dead player. A repeat choice is allowed. Until next dusk, subtract one for each execution vote cast by that player while Thief’s ability works; preserve signed vote arithmetic rather than clamping each step. If Thief dies or is impaired, the modification stops. Exile votes are unaffected.
examples: Thief chooses a voter. During an execution tally, their vote changes the count from three to two.
tipsAndTricksGood: Use your ability to undermine players who you believe are evil! Secretly pick a player you suspect at night, and do not let them know tomorrow that their vote is now negative. When this player votes, they'll be voting with the expectation that they'll be counting towards the vote, when in fact they'll be undermining whatever cause they're working for.

Weaponize your negativity - pick a player you believe to be good, and tell them about it! While this does mean one less good vote on the table, this player now has the very powerful ability to vote against a nomination.

Swap up who you are picking, especially if you're trying to pick evil players. Once a player knows their vote counts negatively, they can use it to their advantage. To avoid this, change who you pick each night, moving the negative vote around and keeping players guessing.

Double and triple bluff who you picked publicly. Players who believe their vote counts negatively will react differently to players who think their vote is normal. With the power of words alone, you can be able to convince an evil player not to vote at a critical juncture.
Remember that you can pick dead players if you want to. This is particularly useful on the final day, since that is when most dead players will be using their single vote.

Keep quiet about who you pick so nobody knows what to expect! This will often mean that players you want to execute, don't get executed, which is an unfortunate downside. However, when each player first votes each day, you can observe their reaction and body language.
If a Bureaucrat is in play, and you think that they are good, co-ordinate with them and both choose the same player, giving a whopping 3 negative votes to a player of your choice.
tipsAndTricksEvil: Pick good players who are figuring out who is good and who is evil, but don't tell them that you have stolen their vote. They will vote for executions that they want to pass, and this will often mean that they are voting for good players.

Lie about who you chose. This will cause confusion and trick the good players into making executions fail when they don't want them to. If a player believes that they have a negative vote, they will vote when they want an execution to fail, but accidentally increase its chances of succeeding instead.

Pick evil players, and tell them that you have picked them. Evil players know exactly who is good and who is evil, so will always use their negative vote effectively. You may need to swap between evil players - choosing the Alpha Wolf one night, then choosing a Minion the next night.

On the final day, you definitely want to choose an evil player, and have them know that you have chosen them. Even if the good team exiles you after the fact, having a negative vote on the Alpha Wolf is incredibly helpful. It may even win you the game!
